# ALGAL

{{SITE_DESCRIPTION}}

ALGAL is a programming language for agents that run for weeks. An ALGAL program is data: a typed graph of steps, model calls, and tools that a host can inspect, hash, and run. A program can pause for an approval, exit, and resume days later on another machine without repeating the work it already did. Every model call and tool result is recorded, so a run can be replayed and checked offline. Programs evolve: ALGAL proposes a candidate, evaluates it against the current version, and adopts the one that scores better. It ships with TypeScript and Rust runtimes that share the same program and record formats. ALGAL is free and open source under the MIT license.

Install the native CLI on macOS (Apple silicon) or Linux (x86_64 and arm64) with `curl -fsSL https://algal.computer/install.sh | sh`; it installs the current GitHub release into ~/.local/bin.

## Pages

- [Write agent programs that outlive the process](https://algal.computer/): a recorded pause-and-resume run, who ALGAL is for, what a program does, how the host runtime records and replays it, and how programs evolve
- [Inside a living program](https://algal.computer/tour/): the guided tour, with recorded runs, interactive diagrams you can replay, source diagnostics, and composition examples
- [Put living programs to work](https://algal.computer/use-cases/): change review, checked coding repairs, portable run histories, reusable routing, and what your host application owns
- [Documentation index](https://algal.computer/docs/): the repository docs rendered for the web, grouped by job: learn the language, run a program, pause and resume, replay, and evolve programs
- [Notes on living programs](https://algal.computer/blog/): longer posts on how the language works, how it is tested, and the design choices behind it
- [Comparisons](https://algal.computer/compare/): how ALGAL compares with LangGraph, BAML, DSPy, Temporal, Restate, and Inngest

## Blog

{{BLOG_POSTS}}

## Comparisons

- [ALGAL vs LangGraph](https://algal.computer/compare/langgraph/): LangGraph's agents are code in your process; ALGAL's programs are typed data a VM runs
- [ALGAL vs DSPy](https://algal.computer/compare/dspy/): DSPy tunes prompts and weights inside a pipeline you design; ALGAL searches over whole programs
- [ALGAL vs Temporal](https://algal.computer/compare/temporal/): Temporal keeps workflow history in its service; ALGAL writes each run to a receipt that verifies offline
- [ALGAL vs Restate](https://algal.computer/compare/restate/): Restate journals handlers inside a Rust server; ALGAL needs no server between invocations
- [ALGAL vs Inngest](https://algal.computer/compare/inngest/): Inngest checkpoints functions on a cloud that bills per step; ALGAL runs from a local binary with no meter
- [ALGAL vs BAML](https://algal.computer/compare/baml/): BAML types LLM functions your app calls; ALGAL runs agent programs that wait, resume, and replay offline

## Limits

- Site examples use scripted model answers. Every run published on the site has a receipt that was replay-checked when the site was built.
- A receipt that verifies shows the run was internally consistent. It does not show that a model's answer is true or that a provider performed an operation.
- Programs can propose new programs as data. The host decides which ones are checked, measured, and kept.
